toastPasteImageFailed: Couldn’t paste the image: {error}. Try again, or drop the image file on the pane.
toastPasteImageDenied: Couldn’t paste the image: Kero can’t write to {dir}. Make it writable, or drop the image file on the pane.
toastPasteImageDiskFull: Couldn’t paste the image: the disk is full. Free some space and try again.
toastPasteClipboardUnreadable: Couldn’t read the clipboard. Copy it again and paste.
toastPasteImageUnsupported: Couldn’t paste the image: {format} isn’t supported. Copy it as PNG or JPEG, or drop the image file on the pane.
toastConfigProblems: {count, plural, one {Your config has # problem: see Settings › Advanced} other {Your config has # problems: see Settings › Advanced}}
cliInstallFailed: Couldn’t install the command line tool
cliAddedToPath: Added the kero command to your PATH: new terminals have it
openProjectMessage: Choose a folder: its sessions are grouped under its name.
confirmCloseSessionDetail: {process} is still running in it. Closing the session ends it.
confirmCloseProjectDetail: {count, plural, one {This ends its # session, with what runs in it.} other {This ends its # sessions, with what runs in them.}}
confirmCloseAllSessionsDetail: {count, plural, one {The project stays; its # session ends, with what runs in it.} other {The project stays; its # sessions end, with what runs in them.}}
confirmClosePaneDetail: {process} is still running in it. Closing the pane ends it.
confirmQuitAllDetail: {count, plural, one {Kero keeps sessions running when it quits. This ends the # session, with what runs in it.} other {Kero keeps sessions running when it quits. This ends all # of them, with what runs in them.}}
restartRunning: {count, plural, one {A program is running in # session} other {Programs are running in # sessions}}
restartStaleDetail: The service that runs your sessions is still Kero {was}, and this is Kero {version}. {running}: restarting ends them, and sessions start again where they were, with their history.
restartServiceDetail: Every pane’s program ends; the shells start again in their folders, under their history.
footerNeedsYou: {count, plural, one {# session needs you} other {# sessions need you}}
footerWorking: {count, plural, one {# session working} other {# sessions working}}
footerDone: {count, plural, one {# session done, unseen} other {# sessions done, unseen}}
footerServiceTip: Sessions run in kerod, in the background: they keep running when you quit kero.
updateRestartTip: Kero was updated: restart the background service to run the new version
updatedDetail: The background service that runs your sessions is from another version. Restart it: your sessions start again where they were, with their history.
emptyDetail: Sessions keep running in the background — quit Kero and come back to everything just as you left it.
paletteRestartServiceDetail: Sessions start again where they were
palettePlaceholder: Go to session or run a command…
paletteNoConversations: No conversations yet. Coding agents’ conversations show here once Kero’s skill is set up for them.
svcRunning: Running (pid {pid}) for {duration} · {sessions, plural, one {# session} other {# sessions}}, {panes, plural, one {# pane} other {# panes}}
svcStale: · still an earlier Kero: restart it to update
setSessionsDetail: Sessions keep running in the background when Kero quits; {action} ends them.
setSessionNameDetail: Until you or an agent name one. With Pane You’re In, a pane running only its shell defers to the pane that needs you most.
setSidebarRowsDetail: Detailed rows add a line under each session’s name: its status message, else its branch and changes.
setFocusFollowsMouseDetail: A pane takes the focus when the pointer moves into it, without a click.
setAskBeforeClosing: Ask before closing a running program
setAskBeforeClosingDetail: When a pane or session you close has a program other than the shell running.
setRestoreSessionsDetail: If the background service stops, as when the Mac restarts, sessions start again in their folders, under their history.
setResumeAgentsDetail: Claude Code, Codex, Pi and OpenCode pick up their conversation where it was, once Kero’s skill is set up for them in Agents.
setAppIconDetail: Closing the window keeps Kero running in the menu bar.
setAutoCheckDetail: Once a day, while Kero is open.
setAutoInstallDetail: They take effect the next time Kero opens.
setTranslucentDetail: Let the desktop show through the window’s background.
setDimUnfocusedDetail: Fade what you’re not in: the panes of the kinds turned on, when a session has several, and the Explorer.
setFontDetail: JetBrains Mono with Nerd Fonts’ icons comes with Kero. Any installed monospaced font works; names separated by commas are tried in order.
setLigaturesDetail: Join characters as the font draws them, as => and !=.
setThickenDetail: A heavier stroke, as Ghostty’s font-thicken.
setColorsDetail: One of Ghostty’s themes, or your own in {dir}, colors the window, its panes and terminals in place of the theme above. Point at a theme to preview it.
setFileColorsDetail: Code in editor panes and the Explorer: in the terminals’ theme, or a theme of its own.
setThemeReplaces: Replaces your theme of this name.
setThemeNameInvalid: A name can’t start with a dot or have / \ : * ? " < > |.
setThemeNameTaken: “{name}” is a theme of Ghostty’s: choose another name.
setOptionMetaDetail: Option sends Alt to programs, as for Emacs and readline, instead of typing accents.
setCopyOnSelectDetail: What you select goes to the clipboard.
setClipboardReadDetail: As with OSC 52: agents asking for what you copied.
setWheelScrollDetail: How far a notch of the wheel scrolls.
setTrackpadScrollDetail: How fast scrolling with two fingers goes.
setShellGroupDetail: Changes apply to panes started after them.
setScrollbackDetail: How much output each pane keeps, also while no window shows it.
setEnvironmentDetail: Added to every pane’s, over what kero sets (TERM, KERO_SESSION…).
setNotifyUnpackaged: This build can’t post notifications: macOS shows those of packaged apps only.
setNotifyWaitingDetail: A program asks something, rings the bell, or reports it is blocked.
setNotifyDoneDetail: While you look at another session, or another app.
setDockBadgeDetail: With the number of sessions that need you.
setDockBounceDetail: Once, when a session comes to need you.
setRemoteControlDetail: kero do and kero focus run the app’s actions, as its menus do: splitting, switching sessions, opening the palette. kero browser clicks, types and reads in browser panes.
setCliDetail: Inside Kero, every pane has the kero command on its PATH already.
setCliNotInstalled: Not installed: other terminals don’t know the kero command.
setSkillsDetail: Teaches agents to start sessions and panes, drive them, wait for them and report their status, and tells them, as they start, which session they’re in.
setProgramStatusDetail: Programs report what they do with OSC 7501, Superlogical’s program status protocol: the sidebar shows it, and notifies you.
setConfigurationDetail: Every setting here is a line of this file, as Ghostty’s: edit it in any editor, and what you save applies at once. kero config show lists every key.
setBackgroundServiceDetail: kerod runs your sessions: quitting kero leaves it running.
setResetDetail: Back to how Kero comes, shortcuts included.
setKeyboardHelp: Click a shortcut, then type the new one. Delete removes it; Escape keeps it.
setShortcutNeedsMac: A shortcut needs ⌘, ⌃ or ⌥, unless it is a function key.
setShortcutNeedsPc: A shortcut needs Ctrl or Alt, unless it is a function key.
splitFileTitle: Open a File in the Pane
setSessionsSideDetail: The side of the window the sessions take. The Explorer, with Changes and Files, takes the other.
setExplorerFolderDetail: What the Explorer's header shows of the folder it shows. Fit shows the path, else the name, as the room allows.
setPaneFolderDetail: What a pane's header shows of the folder it works in. Fit shows the path, else the name, as the room allows.
setFileOpenDetail: In the Files view, as Enter does. A file of another machine opens in a pane.
setFilePaneDetail: A file opened in a pane goes to a new pane, or replaces the file of the file pane you were in last, unless it has unsaved edits.
setFilePreviewDetail: Open the file you choose in the Files view below the tree. Off, a file's menu still has Preview.
setHiddenFilesDetail: Files and folders whose names start with a dot, in the Files view.
changesTurnTip: Changes the agent made since it last started working
changesUncommittedTip: Changes not yet committed, including untracked files
changesBranchTip: Changes on this branch since it branched from {branch}
changesNoneTurn: The agent hasn't changed any files since it started working.
changesNoRepoDetail: A session's changes show here while it works in a git repository.
changesGitOffDetail: Turn on Show Git Status in Settings to see the changes here.
gitIgnoreTrackedDetail: {count, plural, one {Git tracks this file, and keeps tracking it when .gitignore lists it. Stop tracking it to remove it from the repository at the next commit. The file stays on disk.} other {Git tracks # files here, and keeps tracking them when .gitignore lists them. Stop tracking them to remove them from the repository at the next commit. The files stay on disk.}}
changesRevertTip: Put the old lines back in the file
setGitDetail: Branches and changes of the repositories sessions work in.
setGitStatusDetail: Each session's branch and changes, by its panes' titles and in the sidebar.
setDiffLayoutDetail: Auto shows diffs unified while the Explorer is narrow, and side by side once it's wide.
setEditorDetail: What Open in Editor runs with the file's path, as code or zed. Empty opens a file with the app the system opens it with, and a folder with the app it opens text files with.
setBlockAdsDetail: Blocks ads and trackers with filter lists, which Kero downloads and keeps up to date.
setAdListEasylist: Ads, the list most blockers start from.
setAdListPeterLowe: Ad and tracker servers, by their domains.
setAdListFanboyAnnoyance: Pop-ups, newsletter prompts and chat boxes, and the cookie and social lists' too.
setAdListsNote: Lists hide more as they add up, and may break a page now and then. Lists of other URLs go in the configuration, as browser-filter-list.
changesUnmodified: {count, plural, one {# unmodified line} other {# unmodified lines}}
filesNoFolderDetail: A session's files show here while one of its terminals works in a folder.
filesChangedOnDisk: The file changed on disk since you opened it.
filesFilterTip: Finds files and folders by name in all of the folder, or by path with a slash, as src/main. Enter or Down goes to them, Esc clears it.
filesMoreMatches: More match than show. Type more of the name.
filesConfirmCloseDetail: Your edits to {file} aren't saved, and go with the pane.
filesNewFileTip: A name, or a path in the folder, as src/main.go. Enter makes it, Esc leaves it.
filesNotInTree: {path} isn't in the folder the Files view shows
filesNewTip: The file isn't there yet: saving it makes it
hostAuthHint: Kero signs in with your SSH keys and agent, and never asks for a password. To trust a host's key, run ssh {address} once in a terminal.
hostRemoveDetail: Its sessions keep running on {host}. Add the host again to see them.
hostUpdateDetail: Kero then restarts its service on {host}. Sessions there start again where they were, with their history, and the programs running in them end.
hostUpdateAppDetail: The Kero app on {host} updates and relaunches, then restarts its service. Sessions there start again where they were, with their history, and the programs running in them end.
hostUpdateDev: A development build of Kero can't update a host. Run a released Kero, or update the host with kero daemon update there.
hostVersionDetail: {host} runs Kero {version}, and this app is Kero {app}. Update Kero there to see and start its sessions here.
hostDesktopDetail: {host} runs the Kero app, version {version}, and this is Kero {app}. Update Kero on {host}, or turn on Let them update Kero there (Settings › Hosts) to update it from here.
hostRestartDetail: Sessions on {host} start again where they were, with their history, and the programs running in them end.
hostStaleTip: The service on {host} still runs Kero {was}, and Kero {version} is installed there: restart it to run the new version.
pasteNotAFile: Kero pastes files into a pane on another machine, not folders: {name}
pasteTooLarge: Kero pastes at most {size} MB into a pane on another machine
pickerPlaceholder: Filter folders, or type a path: ~/code
pickerHint: ↩ go in · {open} open the folder chosen
setHostsDetail: Other machines whose sessions show in the sidebar after this computer's. Kero reaches them over SSH with your keys and agent, through WSL, or through kerod's listener on your tailnet, and kero -H <name> drives them from the command line.
setHostsNoneDetail: Add a machine you reach with ssh. If Kero isn't installed there, Kero offers to install it.
setHostAddDetail: me@devbox or ssh://me@devbox:2222 over SSH, as ssh takes it with your ~/.ssh/config; wsl://Ubuntu for a WSL distribution; http://devbox:7373 or https://devbox.tail1234.ts.net for kerod's tailnet listener.
setHostRemoteControlDetail: Let programs on {host} show sessions and run the app's actions (kero focus, kero do)
setListenDetail: kerod listens at this computer's Tailscale addresses, for Kero on your other machines. Only your Tailscale account may connect.
setListenOn: Add this computer as a host on your other machines at this address. Only your Tailscale account may connect.
setListenNoTailscale: Tailscale isn't running here: kerod listens once it is.
setRemoteUpdatesDetail: Kero on your other machines can update this app to its version. The app relaunches, and the programs running in its sessions end.
setHostSettingsSplitDetail: The shell, environment, scrollback and session restore of a host's sessions come from its own configuration: run kero config edit on the host. Appearance, keyboard and notifications are this app's.
setShellThisComputer: These apply to this computer's sessions. Each host's come from its own configuration (Settings › Hosts).
confirmQuitAllHosts: Sessions on other machines keep running.
hostInstallDetail: Kero runs its install script on {host}: the server build of Kero goes in your home folder there (~/.local, or %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows), and kerod runs as a service of yours.
hostLinkRefused: Kero opens only web links of {host}, not {scheme} ones
hostManualDetail: {host} runs Kero {version}, and this app is Kero {app}. Update Kero on {host} as you installed it, then restart its service.
hostNewerDetail: {host} runs Kero {version}, newer than this app's {app}. Update this app to see and start the host's sessions.
hostSameAs: This host's kerod is {other}'s, which the app shows already
browserBlank: Type an address or a search above
worktreeDetailDefault: Kero checks out a new branch from the default branch in a folder of its own, so the session’s agent works apart from the others.
worktreeDetailCurrent: Kero checks out a new branch from the current branch in a folder of its own, so the session’s agent works apart from the others.
worktreeRemoveMerged: Its folder {path} goes, and its branch {branch}, which is merged.
worktreeRemoveUnmerged: Its folder {path} goes. Its branch {branch} stays, with its commits.
worktreeRemoveDirty: {count, plural, one {# changed file} other {# changed files}} in {path} will be lost. Its branch {branch} stays, with its commits.
setSessionHistoryDetail: List the coding agents' ended conversations in the sidebar, to resume them later or archive them.
endedDeleteAllDetail: Kero forgets them; each agent keeps its own history of the conversation.
endedSetUpSkill: Set up Kero's skill for your agents to list their ended conversations here
toastGlobalShortcutFailed: Couldn’t use {keys} for the quick terminal: {error}
setCommitMessageDetail: The command that writes a commit message of what's staged. It runs in your shell and gets the prompt on its standard input. '{session}' in it becomes the ID of the pane agent's conversation, to fork it. Empty forks that conversation with the agent's own command.
gitAgentWorkingDetail: {action} changes files the agent may be editing. Run it when the agent is done, or now?
gitAgentWorkingNow: {action} changes a file the agent may be editing.
gitWaiting: {action} is waiting for the agents here to finish
gitPublishTip: Publish Branch: push it to the remote and track the remote branch
gitSyncTip: Sync with {upstream}: pull its commits, then push yours
gitPushForceDetail: Commits on {upstream} that this branch doesn't have are lost. If someone pushed to it since your last fetch, the push stops instead.
gitNewBranchDetail: Starts from the current commit and keeps your changes.
gitUndoCommitDetail: Its changes return as staged changes.
gitBranchFilter: Find a branch, or type a new name
gitDeleteBranchDetail: Its commits stay on the other branches that contain them.
gitDeleteUnmergedDetail: Deleting it loses those commits. Git's reflog keeps them for a while.
gitSwitchDirtyDetail: Stash {count, plural, one {the changed file} other {the # changed files}} and switch, or bring them to {name} if they don't conflict.
gitResolveFirst: {count, plural, one {Resolve the conflict first} other {Resolve the # conflicts first}}
gitWriteMessageTip: Write the message with a coding agent
gitWriteMessageFork: Write the message with a fork of {agent}'s conversation, which knows why it made the changes
gitOperationConflicts: {count, plural, one {# conflict stops} other {# conflicts stop}} the {op}. Resolve each one, then mark it resolved.
gitAbortTip: Cancel the {op} and go back to where it started
gitStageChangeTip: Stage this change for the next commit
gitUnstageChangeTip: Remove this change from the next commit
gitDeleteDetail: It's untracked, so git can't restore it.
gitRestoreDetail: It returns to its staged version.
gitDiscardAllDetail: {count, plural, one {The file returns to its staged version, or is deleted if untracked.} other {The # files return to their staged versions, and untracked files are deleted.}}
mergeConflictsLeft: {count, plural, =0 {All conflicts resolved} one {# conflict left} other {# conflicts left}}
gitUseSideDetail: The file becomes {name}'s version and is marked resolved. Its conflict markers and any edits since the conflict are lost.
gitResolveWithAgentTip: Ask the agent in this worktree to resolve the conflicts and stage them
gitAgentSendFailed: Couldn't send the conflicts to the agent: {error}
gitMergeIntoNoFF: Merge {name} into {branch} with a Merge Commit
gitRebaseDetail: Commits on {branch} that {name} doesn't have are replayed on top of {name}. If {branch} was already pushed, it then needs a force push.
gitRebaseStashDetail: {count, plural, one {The changed file is} other {The # changed files are}} stashed first and restored when the rebase ends. If they conflict, they stay in the stash.
rebasePickTip: Keep the commit as it is
rebaseRewordTip: Keep the commit, with a new message
rebaseEditTip: Stop at the commit to change it, then continue
rebaseSquashTip: Combine the commit with the one below it, and keep both messages
rebaseFixupTip: Combine the commit with the one below it, and keep only that one's message
rebaseHelp: Drag commits to reorder them, the newest on top. Keys: P Pick, R Reword, E Edit, S Squash, F Fixup, D Drop; Alt+↑ and Alt+↓ move a commit.
rebaseBackup: Back up the current state to a temporary branch
rebaseNothing: {branch} has no commits that {commit} doesn't have.
rebaseSquashFirst: {action} needs a kept commit below it
rebaseAllDropped: Keep at least one commit, or reset the branch instead
gitChangeMoved: The change was updated. Review it and try again.
historyNoneDetail: The branch's commits show here as a graph.
historyMoreFound: More commits match than are shown. Refine the filter.
historyFilterTip: Filter commits by message, author or hash
historyFirstParent: First Parent Only: show each merge as one commit
historyResetSoftDetail: The later commits become staged changes.
historyResetMixedDetail: The later commits become unstaged changes.
historyResetHardDetail: The later commits and all uncommitted changes are lost.
gitStageLinesTip: Stage the selected lines for the next commit
gitUnstageLinesTip: Remove the selected lines from the next commit
gitDiscardLinesTip: Discard the changes to the selected lines
searchTip: Finds the agents' conversations by what was said in them, their titles and folders. Narrow it with agent:codex, dir:kero or date:<2d, and leave out what has a word with -word. ↑↓ choose, Enter resumes, Esc clears.
searchTurns: {count, plural, one {You wrote # message} other {You wrote # messages}}
searchRestart: Kero's service runs an older version, which can't search. Restart it to search this machine's conversations.
searchRestartHost: {host} runs an older Kero, which can't search. Update it to search its conversations.
setResumeCommandsDetail: The command that resumes each agent's conversations, as Resume, the search and restoring sessions start them. It runs in your shell, as your own commands and functions do, as cc --yolo --resume '{session}'; '{session}' in it becomes the conversation's ID. Empty uses the agent's own command.
goToFileNoFolder: No folder to find files in: open a session in one
goToFileHint: Enter opens it, {keys} in a pane of its own
goToFileMore: {count, plural, one {Only # file is listed} other {Only the first # files are listed}}: type to find among them
searchNoFolderDetail: Search finds text in the files of the folder of the pane you're in, as Files shows them.
searchResults: {count, plural, one {# result} other {# results}} in {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
searchResultsMore: The first {count, plural, one {# result} other {# results}}, in {files, plural, one {# file} other {# files}}
searchNoneDetail: No line of the folder's files has {query}.
reviewCommentTip: Comment on the lines selected of this change, or on all of it, for the agent to address
reviewTitle: {count, plural, one {# review comment} other {# review comments}}
reviewDiscardTitle: {count, plural, one {Discard the review comment?} other {Discard # review comments?}}
reviewSendTip: Paste the comments as one prompt in the pane of the agent in this worktree, and send it
reviewNoAgent: No agent works in this worktree
reviewSendFailed: Couldn't send the review to the agent: {error}
reviewSent: {count, plural, one {# comment} other {# comments}} sent to {agent}
